central_node: National Identity, Cultural Unity in Diversity, and Conservation Duties

key_details: Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950
Celebrated annually nationwide as Republic Day
Establishes democratic equality and civic duties
real_world_examples: Republic Day parade in New Delhi

key_details: Mandates that every Indian citizen must protect nature
Requires safeguarding forests, lakes, rivers, and wild animals
real_world_examples: School tree planting and wildlife preservation drives

key_details: Regional headgear varieties reflect geographic traditions
Language panel on Indian currency notes displays 15 regional languages
Demonstrates official constitutional recognition of diversity
real_world_examples: Turbans, topis, and phetas across states
Language panel on Indian rupee banknotes

key_details: Ancient Indian philosophy meaning 'the world is one family'
Promotes universal empathy, peaceful co-existence, and global care
real_world_examples: Cultural exchange festivals celebrating national heritage

key_details: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the sole home of Asiatic lions
Forest guards and local pastoralists protected endangered lions
Successfully rescued Asiatic lions from near extinction
real_world_examples: Gir Forest Asiatic lion population recovery
